map: LedgerLock reference fixture — requirement -> reference behaviour -> acceptance assertions -> mutants (WP-2.0.3); closed over every section of REQUIREMENTS.md

requirements.heading: Purpose
requirements.reason: purpose statement; the behaviours it names are R-3..R-9

requirements.heading: Non-Goals
requirements.reason: non-goals; the absence of network, server, UI and database is the shape of the reference, not a measured behaviour (R-12 measures the side-channel half)

requirements.heading: Key normalization (Unicode NFC)
requirements.behaviour: every key is NFC before storage, lookup, hashing and serialisation; NFD and NFC spellings are one key

requirements.heading: JSONL hash chain
requirements.behaviour: one JSONL line per mutation with hash = SHA-256(prev_hash || '|' || canonical bytes with hash and prev_hash blank); the first prev_hash is the literal GENESIS; lines are appended, never rewritten
requirements.interpretation: canonical bytes = JSON with sorted keys, no whitespace, non-ASCII kept; the constant is the literal string GENESIS

requirements.heading: Tamper evidence
requirements.behaviour: a full recomputation from disk detects a mutated value, a swapped op, a modified hash and a broken link, reporting the first bad index; a clean chain is ok

requirements.heading: Independent verify
requirements.behaviour: verify reads the chain from disk and consults nothing the instance remembers, so a tamper after the same instance appended is detected

requirements.heading: Request IDs
requirements.behaviour: a rid is a non-empty string; an empty rid is refused (ValueError; CLI exit 2) and nothing is written

requirements.heading: Idempotency
requirements.behaviour: a replayed rid returns the same result and appends nothing
requirements.interpretation: a rid is replayed when any committed line carries it, whatever its op or key

requirements.heading: Conflict
requirements.behaviour: a different rid on a key whose last committed mutation used another rid raises ConflictError (CLI exit 4) and appends nothing

requirements.heading: Tombstones
requirements.behaviour: a delete is a tombstone line; a put with a different rid conflicts against it; a put with the tombstone's rid is a no-op returning the delete's result; the key is absent from the snapshot

requirements.heading: Key-with-different-rid-different-op semantics
requirements.behaviour: put with r1 then delete with r2 conflicts; replays of the committed put do not conflict

requirements.heading: Atomic Batch Mutation
requirements.behaviour: a batch is planned against the chain and itself, then written as a whole through a sibling temp file, fsync and rename: all lines or none; a conflict anywhere commits nothing; a replay inside the batch appends once
requirements.interpretation: the CLI batch file is a JSON list of {op, key, value, rid, ts}; 'under the lock' is single-process serialisation (no threading module is allowed by R-10); a crash cannot be injected from outside, so atomicity is measured by its observable postconditions (bytes unchanged on refusal, old bytes a prefix on success, no temp sibling left)

requirements.heading: Deterministic Snapshot
requirements.behaviour: the snapshot holds the latest committed put per key unless tombstoned, keys sorted in UTF-8 byte order, byte-stable across calls; the CLI writes the same bytes

requirements.heading: Repair-tail
requirements.behaviour: a truncated final line is removed and the chain verifies afterwards; a clean chain is a no-op; corruption not confined to the tail is refused with the file untouched
requirements.interpretation: truncated = the final line is unterminated and does not parse or hash; a complete last line that fails its hash is corruption, refused

requirements.heading: Durability
requirements.behaviour: every function that opens the ledger for writing flushes and fsyncs before it returns
requirements.interpretation: durability cannot be observed from outside the process; the assertion reads the source of the tree

requirements.heading: CLI Exit Codes (exact contract)
requirements.behaviour: exit 0 on success, 2 on a usage error, 3 on an I/O error, 4 on a conflict, 5 on corruption (verify not ok, repair-tail refusal)

requirements.heading: Language / Runtime
requirements.behaviour: imports only the allowed standard-library modules; ledger.py and cli.py start with `from __future__ import annotations`
requirements.interpretation: the negative witness is a used import of a module outside the allowed set (M-10-1, two inserted lines: the import and its use)

requirements.heading: Tests and Coverage
requirements.reason: unit tests, 85% coverage and runner agreement are requirements on the product's own test suite; ProductProof never depends on developer tests (invariant IX) and this fixture measures product behaviour only; the mapping of test-named criteria is the DECISION-3 domain

requirements.heading: No Side Channels
requirements.behaviour: no socket, no subprocess, no os.system in the tree; the only files touched are the ledger, the batch input and the snapshot output
requirements.interpretation: the negative witness is an os.system call in the write path (M-12-1); the file-access half is a property of the reference's design (its opens name only those paths) and has no separate mutant

requirements.heading: Repository layout
requirements.behaviour: the package has __init__.py, ledger.py (Ledger, ConflictError, append, verify, snapshot, apply_batch) and cli.py; the imported package resolves inside the tree under evaluation
requirements.interpretation: the negative witness for the layout half is M-13-1 (ledger.py no longer defines apply_batch; the package re-exports a renamed function under that name); the in-tree resolution half cannot be violated by a product tree under python -I isolation and is witnessed by a harness calibration (the harness importing another tree is rejected by A-13-a). __main__.py is added so that `python -m ledgerlock` (R-9) runs; tests/, docs/, README and pyproject are the product repository's concern, not the reference's

requirements.heading: Acceptance
requirements.reason: items 1-4 and 6 are measured by the assertions named; item 5 (coverage) is R-11
